description: How a chat turn is routed (QA-8, LAT1 control-plane 05 §5): durable (the loop; codeTask when it may hand off to an engine child, CTL-6), engine (an engine run admitted before CTL-6), legacy (today's loop, with its reason) or refused (with its code), as RunAdmissionService answers it through its RoutingDecider. The single source for routing tests and the e2e oracle: Node runs every vector and random inputs against each RoutingDecider adapter (tests/modules/agent-harness/support/routing-vectors.ts), Python evaluates the rules for the oracle (scripts/routing_table.py). Inputs are the levels of `factors` that satisfy `constraints`; the answer is the `then` of the first rule whose `when` matches (each named factor's level is in its list). There is no catch-all rule: an input no rule matches has no answer, which the totality properties catch.

factors.notes: web = the web app's session; api_pat / api_oauth = API clients on the same chat routes; slack and mcp = the external surfaces; schedule = a schedule's firing (no person waits on it).
agent = an agent's route (agentKey from the URL); assistant = the built-in assistant.
The body's chatMode as sent; other = any value no mode names (the public chat routes refuse one at validation).
The org rollout (HarnessRolloutSettings): one switch off at a time; infrastructure_unavailable is what a standalone MongoDB gives.
any = no family list; allowed / not_allowed = the turn's model family is / is not on the list; unresolved = a list, and the model's family cannot be resolved; none = an empty list.
request = a new conversation the request creates in a project; record = the conversation's record is in a project (whatever the body says).
existing = a conversation with no durable turns; durable = one with durable turns.
Whether any worker was seen lately (LIVENESS_FEATURE).
all = a live worker advertises agent_code (the code sandbox is proven); base = none does.

The agent definition's engine profile names this engine; for the assistant's Agent mode, the coding engine the person chose, else the org's default (ENGPICK); none = a loop agent, or no engine chosen.
admits = the org ceiling admits the agent's engine; widens = it admits another engine only; unreadable = the ceiling cannot be read; image_missing = the sandbox broker has no image for the engine.

The body's harness field: none = absent; durable = the turn asks for the durable harness (ASSIST1, read by the assistant's Agent mode only); legacy = the person's chat switch asks for the classic path (CTL-7), honoured for a conversation with no durable turns unless the agent names an engine.

e2e.description: How a row of the e2e options matrix (docs/test-plan/data/e2e-factors.json) maps onto a routing input: defaults, then modes[mode], paths[path], engines[engine], triggers[trigger]. The oracle reports an engine route as durable, with executor engine:<kind>.
